Braided hair is a common occurrence in the [[Westlands]], though in some cultures it holds a special social significance.
==Two Rivers==
[[file:Nynaeve.jpg|thumb|190px|right|Nynaeve's Two Rivers style Braid]]
In the [[Two Rivers]] district of western [[Andor]], women of marriageable age fix their hair into a single braid which often extends down the length of their back. In each village of the region, the local [[Women's Circle]] decides when a girl is mature enough to marry and fix her hair accordingly. Girls as young as fourteen have been known to braid their hair though the average age for a girl is around eighteen years. In {{Ne|998}} [[Egwene al'Vere]] was granted permission by the women's Circle of [[Emond's Field]] to braid her hair at the age of seventeen,{{Ref/book|1|3}} though she began to wear her hair loose after she left the Two Rivers the same year. [[Nynaeve al'Meara]] also left the Two Rivers around the same time but continued to wear her hair in the braided Two Rivers fashion.

==Aiel==
Among the [[Aiel]], braided hair is common amid young girls under the age of twelve. Children typically wear two braids, one over each ear which are frequently entwined with ribbons.{{Ref/book|4|49}} Within Aiel culture, braided hair is a sign of childhood and is it not unheard of for adult women to be required to braid their hair to discharge [[Toh]] incurred from acting immature. The [[Wise One]] [[Amys]] once ordered Egwene al'Vere to braid her hair as a punishment for disobedience during her training to become a [[dreamer]].{{ref/book|4|35}}

==Seanchan==
In the [[Kaensada|Kaensada Hills]] of [[Seanchan]], tribesmen wear a their hair in a long braid as a sign of strength and bravery. To cut off one's braid, as [[Ajimbura]] did in deference to [[Karede]], is to declare oneself a coward among one's own tribe.{{Ref/book|11|36}}

[[file:Ryne Venamar.jpg|thumb|left|150px|Arafellin braids]]
==Arafel==
[[Arafel]]lin men, until their hair is too thin, are known to wear their hair in two braids, one over each ear. Frequently bells are threaded through the braids.{{Ref/book|8|Prologue}}{{ref/book|0|7}}

==Malkier==
The traditions of [[Malkier]] involve a man sitting at the feet of his ''[[carneira]],'' meaning first lover, to weave a cord-like braid of his own hair called a ''[[daori]].'' The hair is cut off at shoulder length after their first night together and the braid is kept by the ''carneira.'' She will present the ''daori'' to the man's bride on his wedding day. Custom dictates that while a man holds his ''daori'' his is at the whim of his ''carneira.''{{ref/book|0|22}}

==Tarabon==
It is fashionable in [[Tarabon]] for women to wear their hair in a multitude of thin braids, which are often beaded.{{ref/book|4|52}}{{ref/book|6|24}}
